topic.chapter_title: Introduction to Computers, Programs, and Java

sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Welcome to Java programming! This chapter is your first step into the world of coding. You'll get a taste of what Java can do and how it works.

• How Java connects to the web and why it's so popular
• The tools you need to write Java programs (JDK, IDEs, etc.)
• How to write, run, and debug your first Java program

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
Think of Java like a recipe book. The *Java Language Specification* is the rulebook (like grammar for a language). The *JDK* is your kitchen (tools to cook). The *IDE* is your smart kitchen assistant (helps you write recipes faster).

Java is special because:
• It runs on almost any device (like a universal recipe that works everywhere)
• It’s secure (your recipes won’t accidentally poison anyone)
• It’s used everywhere—from phones to banks!

Here’s what makes Java tick:
• **Syntax**: The grammar rules of Java (like how to write a sentence)
• **Compilation**: Turning your code into something the computer understands (like translating your recipe into machine language)
• **Execution**: Running your program (like following the recipe to bake a cake)

sections.title: Code Examples
Key Points
points: Java is a high-level, object-oriented programming language developed by Sun Microsystems
The chapter covers computer hardware, software, programming languages, and Java basics
Java programs are compiled to bytecode and run on the Java Virtual Machine (JVM)
JDK, JRE, and IDE are the essential tools for Java development
Understanding the compilation-execution cycle is fundamental before writing programs

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: Java is a powerful, versatile programming language. You need the JDK to write and run Java programs. Start with simple programs like `HelloWorld` to practice.
